claims.claim: Anyone who disagrees with any HMRC decision can appeal to the tax tribunal.
claims.quote: You can appeal to the First-tier Tribunal (Tax) if you want to challenge some decisions by: HM Revenue and Customs ( HMRC )
claims.note: The tribunal accepts some HMRC decisions, not every HMRC decision; direct tax cases must first be appealed to HMRC.

claims.claim: Income Tax, VAT and PAYE decisions can be appealed.
claims.quote: Direct tax includes: Income Tax PAYE Tax Corporation Tax Capital Gains Tax National Insurance contributions Inheritance Tax Indirect tax includes: VAT

claims.claim: Some HMRC penalties can be appealed.
claims.quote: You may be able to appeal if HMRC : sends you an assessment for duty charges you a penalty

claims.claim: An appeal following an HMRC review conclusion must be made within 30 days.
claims.quote: The time limit is 30 days from: the view of the matter letter – direct tax the assessment or decision – indirect tax a review conclusion letter – either indirect or direct tax

claims.claim: There is no filing fee for most tax tribunal appeals.
claims.quote: There is no fee for appealing to the First-tier Tribunal.
